name: Marinus of Neapolis
bio: Marinus of Neapolis is one of the epigrammatists whose short poems were gathered in the Greek Anthology. Paton's index of authors dates the poet to 5th century AD.
This archive carries the 2 epigrams ascribed to the poet in the third volume of W. R. Paton's prose translation (Book IX: 196, 197).

poems.title: Book IX, 196: On the “Life of Proclus”
poems.author: Marinus of Neapolis
poems.text: Marinus, who ever doth works pleasing to the gods, wrote this, too, with pious intent.

poems.title: Book IX, 197
poems.author: Marinus of Neapolis
poems.text: Proclus of blessed memory, this, too, is an excellent deed on the part of thy divine self, that as a saviour and protector of souls in place of thy divine self thou hast left Marinus, the living image of all the immortals, the help of pious men. He, proclaiming the story of thy life, with which God was well pleased, wrote this book as a record of thy virtues for posterity.
